original.title: Helping construction continue puts Native cultural ties to ancestral places and burial traditions at risk.
original.pro_html:
Point 1 Helping construction continue puts Native cultural ties to ancestral places and burial traditions at risk.

  • Because The current financing creates a stopping point. Water district board president Bill Long explains the bill's importance: “Without this legislation there will be a point where we will have to stop.” [8]
  • Because The project's environmental review identifies prehistoric sites in the area it could affect: “Archaeological resources also include two prehistoric sites.” [9]
  • Because The review also records a tie to living tribes: “PA consulting parties, including all invited Indian Tribes, are as follows” [9], a list that includes the “Comanche Nation” [9].
  • Because The review treats encountering undisturbed historic places as a construction risk. Its route plan aims “to diminish the probability of encountering any undisturbed historic properties.” [9]
  • Because It does not guarantee avoiding every burial: “All known burials or cemeteries will be avoided to the extent possible.” [9]
  • So Easing the financial barrier helps more construction proceed with a remaining risk to ancestral places and graves.
  • Because These places matter to living cultures. The National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers explains: “Connections to cultural heritage sustain the health and vitality of Native peoples.” [10]
  • Because Disturbing graves can violate the beliefs expressed through burial traditions. Southern Ute preservation official Cassandra Atencio explains: “When you put somebody in the ground, you expect them to stay there because you made prayers or did something over them, and that meant something so they could go somewhere else. When you uncover that, you're disturbing them, and now you're bringing them back.” [11]
  • Because Listening to and accepting people with different beliefs gives weight to their cultural ties and burial practices, even when [NAME] does not share those beliefs.
  • So Respecting those practices gives [NAME] a reason to oppose financing that advances this risk of disturbance.
  • Note The objection concerns disturbance itself. The plan requires compliance before work restarts: “only when compliance has been completed.” [9] That cannot undo any disturbance that led to discovering a grave.
original.con_html:
Response The PRO does not connect the later construction helped by repayment relief to Native graves. This response does not reach the PRO’s concern for ancestral places more generally.

  • Because The environmental review says, “Archaeological resources also include two prehistoric sites.” [9]
  • Because The original environmental impact statement describes what such recorded sites are: “Prehistoric site types include open camps, open stone tool scatters, kill sites, open architectural, and rock art.” [12] It lists “cemeteries” [12] among historic site types.
  • Because The statement’s surveys are incomplete: “These inventories surveyed between 4 and 19 percent of potential affected area.” [12] So the record does not rule graves out; it also does not show them.
  • Because The burial provision addresses a condition: “If a burial or cemetery cannot be avoided or is encountered during construction” [9].
  • So A rule for handling a possible discovery does not establish that this work reaches a Native grave, and the recorded site types do not supply that step.
  • Because Atencio’s account explains the meaning of uncovering a buried person: “When you uncover that, you're disturbing them, and now you're bringing them back.” [11] It is a general account, not a statement about this project.
  • Because Listening to and accepting people gives weight to their beliefs. It does not turn a general account of burial beliefs into evidence that this work would disturb such a burial.
  • So The grave part of the PRO’s reason needs a link to this work that its sources do not supply.
original.notes_html:
Evidence note: The EIS reports 850 cultural resources within a 2-mile buffer across all alternatives, including 55 prehistoric sites and 53 prehistoric isolates, and says inventories surveyed between 4 and 19 percent of the potentially affected area. Inventory results and tribal and state consultations could shift alignments to avoid known sites. On federal or trust land Reclamation follows NAGPRA; on state or private land it follows state unmarked burial law and the programmatic agreement. Work stops if unrecorded resources are found. Sources: [12], [9].

Evidence note: Bill Long said existing funds carry construction for another three to five years and that the repayment problem arises in the second half of the project. The record reviewed does not say which recorded sites lie in that half. Sources: [8].

original.title: Helping replace contaminated water protects against cancer, kidney harm and infections.
original.pro_html:
Point 1 Helping replace contaminated water protects against cancer, kidney harm and infections.

  • Because Communities the conduit would serve have unsafe water sources: “The drinking water sources they rely on are often contaminated with unsafe levels of radium, uranium, and other pollutants.” [5]
  • Because These radioactive substances raise cancer risk: “Exposure to radionuclides from drinking water results in the increased risk of cancer.” [6] EPA also identifies uranium's kidney hazard: “toxic effects to the kidney” [6].
  • Because Some groundwater is affected by surface water that “contains harmful microorganisms and pollutants.” [7]
  • Because Reclamation explains how the new source helps: “The AVC will eliminate or reduce the effects of those contaminants by delivering filtered water from Pueblo Reservoir.” [8]
  • Because Local providers would disinfect the delivered water before it enters household water systems: “AVC Project Participants would be responsible for adding a disinfectant residual (likely free chlorine) at the entry points to their distribution systems.” [7]
  • Because Disinfection protects water on its way to the tap: “This remaining disinfectant kills germs living in the pipes between the water treatment plant and your tap.” [9]
  • So Easier financing helps complete a safer water source, with local disinfection, that reduces cancer, kidney and infection risks for people who drink this water, including any ordinary American living, working or staying in these communities. Preventing disease through everyday drinking water serves [NAME]'s concern for personal health to the extent [NAME] relies on such water.
original.notes_html:
Evidence note: The conduit’s service area is the Lower Arkansas River Valley east of Pueblo, with 39 participating systems and a service population of about 50,000. Both the benefits and the construction hazards fall mainly on people in or passing through that area. The district is the repayment entity. The EPA household-bill findings and the CDC hospital warning are national statements, and the record gives no estimate for a household bill here. CDC’s “Particle pollution can affect anyone” describes who can be harmed, not who meets this dust. Sources: [3], [10].

Evidence note: Sources differ on the number of systems out of compliance. District testimony and the committee chair report 18 systems or communities failing standards for radionuclides. Reclamation’s November 2024 testimony says twelve water providers exceed federal mandatory standards. Sources: [3], [11].

original.title: Helping secure lasting water supplies protects daily hygiene and patient care.
original.pro_html:
Point 2 Helping secure lasting water supplies protects daily hygiene and patient care.

  • Because The existing supply has a reliability problem: “communities in the region continue to face unreliable water supplies and serious water quality challenges.” [5]
  • Because Keeping local treatment working is also a concern. Reclamation warns: “Without a realistic option for the coming decades, these same communities would be unlikely to achieve sustainable water treatment.” [11]
  • Because Treating the old sources creates a further problem: “When this groundwater is cleaned to drinking water standards, in many cases it produces a reject stream which violates EPA discharge standards.” [3] The reject stream is the polluted wastewater left by treatment.
  • So Helping finance the new source supports lasting water service by reducing dependence on costly local treatment with waste-disposal problems.
  • Because Water access supports routine disease prevention: “Lack of access to safe water and sanitation can create obstacles to maintain hygiene and prevent the spread of diseases.” [12]
  • Because The conduit would also supply health facilities: “It would mean water for hospitals in towns such as La Junta, which are keeping Coloradans healthy.” [13]
  • Because Hospitals need dependable water to keep treating patients: “During water system interruptions, the operation of healthcare facilities is severely interrupted and capability can be almost completely degraded within two hours.” [14]
  • So Supporting dependable supplies protects water for drinking, staying clean and receiving safe hospital care for people who use these systems and facilities. These are ordinary personal health needs, and they give [NAME] a reason to favor the bill to the extent [NAME] relies on these services.

original.title: Easing water-cost pressure protects access to water, food and medical care, and reduces a source of stress.
original.pro_html:
Point 3 Easing water-cost pressure protects access to water, food and medical care, and reduces a source of stress.

  • Because Water-system costs reach household bills. EPA explains: “Because projected capital and operational costs for water utilities have increased, utilities often need to raise rates to account for the current and future needs.” [12]
  • So Lower interest and more time to repay ease the annual costs that water providers must cover. That helps limit pressure on water bills as communities secure safe service.
  • Because Unaffordable bills threaten continued access: “Unpaid bills can lead to water disconnections and residential shutoffs, which can force households to rely on unsafe water sources or to forgo essential hygiene practices” [12].
  • Because Water bills also compete with other health needs: “High water bills can force families to cut back on other essential expenses, such as food, healthcare, and education.” [12] EPA identifies “underutilization of healthcare and medications, food insecurity” [12] among the resulting health harms.
  • Because Insecure water access also harms mental health: “Water insecurity and inadequate sanitation contribute to poorer mental health and have been linked to increased depression and anxiety.” [12]
  • So Easing these pressures helps households on these water systems keep safe water, protect nutrition and medical care, and avoid water-related stress. Those health protections serve [NAME]'s wish to be secure and avoid disease to the extent [NAME] pays such bills.

original.title: Helping finish construction brings dust that can irritate eyes and airways.
original.pro_html:
Point 1 Helping finish construction brings dust that can irritate eyes and airways.

  • Because The 2022 plan includes rural pipeline work: “construction of additional delivery pipelines will result in increased short-term construction disturbances in rural areas.” [7]
  • Because The project review identifies dust from digging and requires controls: “A control plan for fugitive dust would be developed and implemented to minimize particulate and dust emissions during earth work.” [15]
  • Because Construction dust has health effects: “Larger particles, called PM10, irritate the eyes, nose, and throat. Dust from roads, farms, dry riverbeds, construction sites, and mines are types of PM10.” [10]
  • Because This concern applies to ordinary people: “Particle pollution can affect anyone” [10].
  • So Easing the payment barrier helps the remaining work go ahead, along with its dust emissions. Avoiding that exposure serves [NAME]’s wish to protect health to the extent [NAME] lives near or passes through the work.
